Final state verified — solution.py is byte-identical to the version that passed all 5 shapes remotely (status: correct, peak_fraction 0.1755): a fused Triton W4A16 kernel that views the packed uint8 weights as int32 for 16B-vectorized loads, unpacks 8 nibbles per word in registers, dequantizes per 128-group with bf16 scales/zero-points, accumulates on tensor cores in fp32, and uses SPLIT_K + an fp32-partials reduce kernel to keep all 188 SMs busy on decode shapes, with per-shape autotuning frozen into low-overhead direct launches.

The last (6th) run tried a redesigned kernel (interleaved full-width dots + exact-integer s·(dot−z·Σx) epilogue); it passed shapes 0–1 but failed shape 2 on an untestable specialization path, so I reverted to the proven file rather than ship an unverifiable fix.

One-line summary: Fused Triton int4→bf16 W4A16 GEMM with int32-vectorized nibble unpack, tensor-core fp32 accumulation, autotuned tiles, and split-K for decode shapes — verified correct on all 5 target shapes on the RTX PRO 6000 at 0.1755 peak fraction (best decode ≈460 GB/s, prefill ≈122 TFLOPs).
